requirements: NIP client certificate validation to configured trust anchors
certificate NID binding to the post-Caps IdentFrame
NCP-NID-MISMATCH rejection before forwarding a mismatched IdentFrame

historical_items.disposition: No rate-limit algorithm or quota contract is defined by NPS-RFC-0006. Deployments may compose an edge limiter or an authenticated Anchor policy without changing the transport contract.
NeuronHub customer authentication is a managed-product concern, not an open NPS transport requirement. Native NPS identity remains NIP mTLS plus IdentFrame binding.

AaaS L2-03 applies CGN-Estimate to service responses and L3-08 applies CGN-Billing only to commercial settlement flows. A byte-transparent TLS terminator neither produces service responses nor claims a settlement flow.
AaaS L2-09 is a SHOULD for deployments claiming the AaaS L2 profile. nps-ingress does not claim that profile or publish an NWM; an Anchor deployment may enforce RFC-0005 behind this transport edge.

NPS-CR-0001 defines Anchor as a protocol role, not a mandatory responsibility of the nps-ingress process. This daemon proxies admitted NCP sessions to the configured backend and does not claim Anchor behavior.

The current NPS protocol defines framing and handshake bounds, which are enforced here. Volumetric protection, request-rate caps and fail2ban integration are deployment controls and are not advertised as daemon capabilities.

claim: nps-ingress claims only the RFC-0006 transport admission boundary and the listed local framing/time bounds; it does not claim AaaS, Anchor, billing, reputation, customer-authentication, rate-limit, or full DDoS capabilities.
